evidence.title: Tool use enables construction of a covert communication channel
evidence.observation: Authors report tool-assisted covert-channel implementation by Claude Opus 4.6, including a hidden implementation missed by an Opus monitor. This is supplied-task capability construction, not spontaneously adopted collusion.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality
evidence.limitations: Complete coordination index was zero for undetectable conditions; a malicious-paper prompt-injection experiment failed. Small implementation sample; Anthropic-only models; LLM assessment with initial manual checks. Coordination is estimated from plans, not live interoperability trials; zero estimates do not prove impossibility.
evidence.open_questions: Repeated interaction, shared artifacts, cross-provider transfer and real deployment frequency remain unestablished here.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed research finding; not independently reproduced by the Commons.
evidence.dispute_status: No explicit correction located in bounded search; not a systematic retraction clearance
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Capability feasibility progression
terms.definition: An analytical sequence for describing distinct levels of practical possibility: possible → practical → repeatable → scalable. A step need not follow the preceding one automatically, and the categories are not a universal maturity model.

terms.name: Constraint compression
terms.definition: A reduction, often AI-enabled, in the practical barriers of knowledge, expertise, labor, cost, time, or coordination that once limited an activity. It describes the change in constraints, not the eventual impact of the activity.

relationships.explanation: Reduced a specified construction barrier, not all coordination barriers.
Construction capability does not establish reliable or scalable coordination.
